fix on issue/1056-fidelity-flag-gaps · PR #1127 (stacked on #1064) · pinned by fidelity_copies::{a_stock_copy_keeps_its_flag_when_its_source_is_deleted, the_copy_follows_its_source_through_updates_and_setup_clones, the_copys_flag_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_copy_adopts_its_source, the_named_refusal_wins_over_a_gouge_line_the_sim_would_read, the_eyes_colours_are_gated_at_the_tightened_verdict_tolerance} · merges after #1064

Points 1, 3 and 4 are done. Point 2 is partly done: a stock from a #911-era file takes its source's flag on load.

**Still owed (why the PR says Refs, not Fixes):** projects saved before #911. #911 did not bump the project version, so a pre-#911 file with a coarse STEP mesh cannot be told apart from a later file whose models are all fine. Re-measuring on load is not possible either, because the chord error needs the B-rep, which the file does not keep. A proper fix is file-format work (effort:max):
- Bump `PROJECT_VERSION` to 59.
- Mark every model of a v<=58 file "fidelity unknown", and save that mark so re-saving the file cannot turn it into "fine".
- Then the maintainer decides between two options: refuse those models' operations by name until they are re-imported (safe, but it refuses every existing project once), or show a named, non-blocking line.

The details are in docs/decisions/1056-fidelity-flag-gaps.md on the PR branch.
